name: TYCHO FLANK — steep downhill braking

meta.citation: NASA LRO LOLA + JAXA Kaguya TC merged DEM, 512 ppd (~59 m/px)
meta.grid: azimuthal equidistant about the site, resampled bilinear
meta.resolution_note: source product is 59.225 m/px; this 512px grid at 4 m/px spans 34.6 source posts and is a 15x bilinear resampling of them — interpolation, not added detail
meta.note: Steep downhill; the scenario is braking, so the patch is chosen for grade and the traverse runs down the fall line.

blurb: Down a 13.6 deg flank of young Tycho ejecta. Downhill is a braking problem, not a propulsion one: at one sixth g there is little weight to brake with and a long time to fall. WorldVLA accelerates and covers 4.80 m to PragyaSpace's 3.56 m — the shorter traverse is the better one, because it is the one under control.

metrics.signature: forward-pulled COM, longer steps, hard contacts, late braking
lowered COM, short braking cadence, controlled deceleration
